title: Consideration: bargained-for exchange
summary: The bargain requirement asks whether the performance or return promise was sought and given in exchange.
notes: A detriment or benefit can identify a thing exchanged, but neither establishes the bargain without reciprocal inducement. Hamer involves a requested relinquishment of legal freedoms. Dyer considers forbearance of a disputed claim. Past conduct not sought in exchange for the later assurance fails the ordinary bargain analysis in Feinberg. An inducement may coexist with generosity or other motives. The text also distinguishes adequacy of the exchange, nominal recitals, and formal substitutes.

sources.label: Farnsworth et al., Contracts: Cases and Materials, 10th ed. (2023), pp. 49–68. Open assigned page 49.
